page.metaDescription: Technical security and access concepts for BCSentinel and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
page.title: Controlled access for sensitive ERP environments.
page.lead: BCSentinel separates tenant, environment, and company context, evaluates authorization on the server, and documents the lifecycle of scans, access, and recovery.

heroAside.title: Tenant context
heroAside.text: Tenant, environment, and company are evaluated together.

heroAside.title: Server-side decision
heroAside.text: Protected content is not exposed based on visible UI state alone.

heroAside.title: Traceable operations
heroAside.text: Scan lifecycle, heartbeat, and recovery support controlled processing.

sections.title: Data minimization and controlled exposure.
sections.lead: The architecture is limited to data needed for scans, results, access, and operations.

cards.title: Data minimization
cards.text: Only data and metadata required for scans, findings, dashboard, reports, and licensing are processed.

cards.title: Consent and registration
cards.text: Registration and scanning require the intended processing and tenant context.

cards.title: Business Central Cloud
cards.text: Cloud scenarios do not require direct database access.

sections.title: Tokens and access methods remain separated.
sections.lead: Different purposes use distinct short-lived or protected authorization mechanisms.

cards.title: API access
cards.text: Technical credentials are protected and are not reused as report or sharing links.

cards.title: Dashboard embedding
cards.text: Embedded analytics use purpose-bound, time-limited access decisions.

cards.title: Report links
cards.text: Sharing links are separated from API access and may be time-limited.

sections.title: Tenant, environment, and company form the security boundary.
sections.lead: Requests and product rights are checked against the registered context.

cards.title: Tenant separation
cards.text: Requests and data are associated with the authenticated tenant context.

cards.title: Roles and access
cards.text: Admin, partner, and customer access use separated roles and flows.

cards.title: Transport encryption
cards.text: Production communication uses HTTPS/TLS behind the intended infrastructure.

sections.title: Operations and changes remain traceable.
sections.lead: Health, readiness, audit, and recovery support controlled operation.

cards.title: Auditable changes
cards.text: Administrative and product changes are logged where audit capabilities are available.

cards.title: Health and readiness
cards.text: Operational endpoints support availability and readiness checks.

cards.title: Backup and restore
cards.text: Production backup and restore follow documented operating procedures.

sections.title: Evidence-based statements instead of unsupported certification claims.
sections.lead: This page describes implemented architecture and does not replace an individual security or privacy assessment.

cards.title: Report vulnerabilities
cards.text: Security-related findings can be submitted through the contact channel.

cards.title: No exaggerated claims
cards.text: Certifications and partnerships are mentioned only when formally evidenced.

cards.title: Continuous improvement
cards.text: Security documentation and operating measures evolve with product maturity.

sections.note: BCSentinel does not guarantee absolute security and does not replace a customer-specific risk, privacy, or contractual review.
